# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 111 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 111 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_111_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 10, Chapter 1

**1** After I had written down the commandments and similitudes of the shepherd, the angel of repentance, he came to me and said, "I wish to show you all the things which the Holy Spirit, who spoke with you in the form of the church, showed to you; for that Spirit is the Son of God. **2** But since you were weak in flesh, it was not declared to you through an angel; but when you were strengthened through the Spirit and grew powerful in strength, so that you could also see an angel, the building of the tower was then made manifest to you through the church; and you saw all things well and reverently, not frightened by the presence of an angel." **3** A few days later I saw the Glorious One. He said to me: "What do you seek?" **4** I said to him, "Lord, command the shepherd, the angel of repentance, to depart from my house." **5** "He shall remain with you," he said, "as long as you live." **6** "But why?" I asked. **7** "Because the Lord saw your innocence and simplicity," he said, "and the Lord set great value on your simplicity and your innocence; therefore I was sent to dwell with you always, so that you might be kept from all wickedness and walk in righteousness." **8** "But Lord," I said, "I am greatly honored by your presence and your company." **9** "You speak well; but those who are with you must also be watchful, for those companions will be of great benefit to you." **10** "When then, Lord," I said, "will the tower be completed?" "It is being built," he said, "as you see now; for at this very hour all these things which you see are being accomplished."

---

### Translator's Note
Similitude 10 opens by stepping back to reframe the entire Shepherd: the Spirit who spoke through the Church was the Son of God. The Shepherd's permanent residence with Hermas (v. 5) establishes repentance as a lifelong orientation, not a one-time event. Hermas's simplicity and innocence are the qualities that make him a suitable recipient and herald of this revelation. SOPHIA follows LOGOS throughout.
